issues.title: Projected-constraint minimizer need not be the standard L2 minimizer

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ is a minimizer in $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under normalization $P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \in \mathbb{S}$, then $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}} := \tfrac{\| P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \|_{L^2(\D)} }{ \| u_H^{\mathcal{L}} \|_{L^2(\D)} } u_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ is a minimizer in $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the standard normalization $\tilde{u}_H^{\mathcal{L}} \in \mathbb{S}$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: These are just the Euler-Lagrange equations fulfilled by a minimizer of the energy $E$ on the space $V_H^{\mathcal{L}}$ under the constraint $P_H(u_H^{\mathcal{L}}) \in \mathbb{S}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that any minimizer under the constraint $\|P_Hu\|_{L^2}=1$ becomes a minimizer under $\|u\|_{L^2}=1$ after scalar rescaling. The preceding calculation establishes only the projected-mass eigenproblem, equivalently minimization of $E(v)/\|P_Hv\|_{L^2}^2$. The standard LOD problem minimizes $E(v)/\|v\|_{L^2}^2$. Scaling preserves the direction of a vector, while these two Rayleigh quotients generally have different minimizing directions, so the claimed implication is false.
issues.overall_effect: The old lifted iteration is not shown to compute the standard L2-constrained LOD Ritz minimizer to which the later approximation estimates apply. The definition of the LOD space and the approximation theorem for its independently defined standard minimizer remain intact.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly state that the old fixed point minimizes the projected-mass Rayleigh quotient E(v)/||P_Hv||² and cannot generally be converted into the standard Ritz minimizer by scaling. To retain the intended computation of the standard minimizer, bypass the projected-mass step with a discrete inverse iteration directly on V_H^L: define L_H^{-1}z by (L_H^{-1}z,v)_X=(z,v)_{L²} for every v in V_H^L, use this operator in the update, and normalize in the true L² norm. Its lowest fixed point solves (u,v)_X=λ(u,v)_{L²}, so it is the standard L²-constrained LOD Ritz minimizer to which the existing approximation estimates apply.
issues.why_classification: Scalar rescaling cannot repair the different minimizing directions, so this is not a typographical or routine local inference error. The standard-minimizer guarantee can nevertheless be recovered by a contained replacement construction using the discrete Riesz map on the already defined LOD space, without changing that space or its approximation rates; this is nontrivial but does not require global reconstruction.

issues.title: Phase-direction Hessian identity omits its evaluation point

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is seen by considering the energy curve $\omega \mapsto E(\exp(\ci \omega) \bfu )$, which is constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The second derivative is an operator evaluated at the state and then applied to a direction. Differentiating the constant phase curve requires $E''(\bfu)(\ci\bfu)$ paired with $\bfv$. The old expression $E''(\ci\bfu)$ instead supplies the phase direction where the evaluation point should appear and omits the directional application.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed phase-eigenvector identity is malformed, although the surrounding phase-invariance argument makes its intended meaning unambiguous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the malformed term E''(i u) by the Hessian at the state applied to the phase direction, so the identity reads ⟨E''(u)(i u),v⟩−λ(i u,v)_{L²}=0 for every tangent vector v.
issues.why_classification: The nearby Hessian formula, the established state u, and the phase-invariance argument uniquely force the evaluation point and direction. An intended reader can make this notational correction without altering any inference or supplying new mathematics.

issues.title: Convergence theorem invokes an ill-typed quasi-isolation hypothesis

failure_location.quote: If all other eigenvalues of $E^{\prime\prime}(\bfu)$ are strictly larger than $\bfu$, then $\bfu$ is called {\it locally quasi-isolated} \cite{PHMY24,PHMY242}.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, $\lambda$ is always the smallest eigenvalue of $E^{\prime\prime}(\bfu)$ with corresponding eigenfunction $\ci \bfu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's density-convergence clause assumes a locally quasi-isolated ground state in the sense of the preceding subsection. As printed, that condition requires other scalar eigenvalues of $E''(\bfu)$ to be strictly larger than the vector $\bfu$, for which no relevant order relation is defined. The old source identifies $\lambda$ as the scalar eigenvalue associated with the phase direction, so the meaningful hypothesis is that all other eigenvalues are larger than $\lambda$.
issues.overall_effect: The hypothesis of clause (iv), and hence its density-convergence guarantee, is undefined as printed. Clauses (i)–(iii) are unaffected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of local quasi-isolation, replace the vector u by the scalar phase eigenvalue λ: require every other eigenvalue of E''(u) to be strictly larger than λ, and read clause (iv) under that corrected definition.
issues.why_classification: Eigenvalues cannot coherently be ordered against the vector u, while the immediately preceding sentence explicitly identifies λ as the eigenvalue associated with i u. Thus the old source uniquely determines a one-symbol correction, with no change to the intended hypothesis or proof.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: If all other eigenvalues of $E^{\prime\prime}(\bfu)$ are strictly larger than $\lambda$, then $\bfu$ is called {\it locally quasi-isolated} \cite{PHMY24,PHMY242}.

issues.title: Subsequence eigenvalue limit binds the wrong index

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The sequence of iterates possesses a subsequence \( \{ \bfu^{n_j}\}_{j\in \mathbb{N}}\) that converges strongly to a critical point $\bfu\in \boldS$ of $E$

issues.failure_explanation: Item (iii) introduces the subsequence $\{\bfu^{n_j}\}_{j\in\mathbb N}$, but its eigenvalue formula takes $n\to\infty$ although the displayed term depends only on $j$. Thus the stated limit is not a limit of the announced subsequence. The proof establishes convergence of the analogous quantities indexed by $n_k$ as $k\to\infty$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the eigenvalue characterization in item (iii) is ill-formed; the stated subsequence convergence and critical-point conclusion otherwise use the correct subsequence indexing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the limit binder n→∞ in item (iii) by j→∞, retaining the announced subsequence u^{n_j} throughout the eigenvalue formula.
issues.why_classification: The displayed quantity is indexed only by j, the theorem has just introduced the subsequence indexed by j, and the proof uses the analogous k-indexed limit. The correction is uniquely forced and requires no mathematical repair.

issues.title: Step-size condition does not imply the norm bound used in the induction
issues.failure_explanation: Equation `eq:normenergy` gives $\|\bfu_{\mathrm{pr}}^1-\bfu^0\|_R^2\le 4\tau_0^2E(\bfu^0)$. To infer the strict bound below one used to replace a quartic error term by a quadratic one, the proof needs $4\tau_0^2E(\bfu^0)<1$, equivalently $\tau_0^2<(4E(\bfu^0))^{-1}$. The old non-reciprocal condition does not provide this.
issues.overall_effect: The absorption and induction in `lemma:Rnorm` are not justified as written, so its energy-reduction estimate, the dependent corollary, and the convergence theorem's uses of that estimate lack the stated proof until the smallness condition is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the uniform upper step-size bound so that 4 τ_max² E(u⁰)<1, in addition to the other existing smallness requirements. Equivalently, replace the base-step condition by τ₀²<(4E(u⁰))⁻¹ and use τ_n≤τ_max together with E(uⁿ)≤E(u⁰) in the induction. The lemma, dependent corollary, and convergence theorem then follow with their stated conclusions unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes an invalid inference from its non-reciprocal condition, so the defect is substantive rather than a typo. The repair is nevertheless a short, routine algebraic smallness correction already compatible with the lemma's assertion that τ_max depends on the initial energy; it requires no new lemma and preserves the energy-decay and convergence guarantees.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: if \(\tau_0\) is chosen such that \(\tau_0^2 \, < \, (4\, E(\bfu^0))^{-1}\).
